claim: Changes should be made to through the API; To write to a different window. use the routine waddch() ... is provided
quote: doc/html/ncurses-intro.html:534-542: "Changes should be made to through the API, and then the routine refresh()..." and "To write to a different window. use the routine waddch() (for window-specific addch()) is provided." waddch for a WINDOW is correct per curs_addch.3x, but the printed prose is ungrammatical ("to through", period before "use", dangling "is provided").
earlier: After only seeing "to through" I would already have called the printing wrong; reading the waddch sentence confirms a second independent grammar break.

claim: rearing to get started; halfdelay()is called; if he doesn't respond with in certain time
quote: HOWTO:809: "you must be rearing to get started"; HOWTO:1389: "halfdelay()is called to enable the half-delay mode"; HOWTO:1397: "if he doesn't respond with in certain time". halfdelay() itself is a real API (curs_inopts.3x), but the printed wording has typos/grammar errors.
earlier: Finding "rearing" alone would already show the printed text is not correct English; the other two hits are further confirmation.

claim: Mail links to zmbenhal@netcom.com and esr@snark.thyrsus.com, and a link to adahome.com for the Ada95 binding
quote: ncurses-intro.html:418-424 prints mailto:zmbenhal@netcom.com, mailto:esr@snark.thyrsus.com, and href="http://www.adahome.com" labeled as the Ada95 binding, while the same paragraph directs current contact to bug-ncurses@gnu.org. README describes the in-tree Ada95/ binding, not adahome.com.
earlier: Before opening README I would have treated the emails as merely historical; README makes clear the Ada95 binding lives in-tree, so the adahome.com link as "the Ada95 binding" is not correct.

claim: create_box() puts the corners at x + w and y + h, so a box of width 10 and height 3 is drawn 11 columns wide and 4 rows tall, and the erase loop clears one row and column more
quote: init_win_params sets height=3, width=10. create_box draws corners at (y,x), (y,x+w), (y+h,x), (y+h,x+w) and erase loops j<=y+h and i<=x+w. That spans 11 columns and 4 rows, so the printed example's geometry is off-by-one relative to the stated width/height.
earlier: Reading only the corner mvaddch calls would show x+w/y+h placement; the erase loop bounds confirm the same inclusive error.

claim: printw(string); mvprintw(y, x, string); ...
quote: HOWTO shows "printw(string);" and "mvprintw(y, x, string);". curs_printw.3x prototypes are printw(const char *fmt, ...) and mvprintw(int y, int x, const char *fmt, ...), analogous to printf—not a bare string argument.
earlier: The HOWTO listing alone looks like a simplified API; the man page contradicts treating the first argument as an ordinary string rather than a format.

claim: let me clear few things; It doesn't create any thing; as user press a key; Let's dissect it by line by line
quote: HOWTO:1487-1488 "let me clear few things about windows"; :2237 "It doesn't create any thing on the screen actually"; :2366-2369 "as user press a key" and "Let's dissect it by line by line."
earlier: Any one of these phrases already shows defective printed English; the others match the claim's list.

claim: If the terminal does not have such characters, curses.h will map them to a recognizable (though ugly) set of ASCII defaults
quote: ncurses-intro.html:803-805 attributes the ASCII fallback to curses.h. curs_addch.3x: "curses uses the ACS default listed below if the terminal type lacks the acs_chars (acsc) capability". lib_acs.c:_nc_init_acs sets real_map['l']='+', etc. The header defines ACS_* names; the library performs the mapping.
earlier: Without lib_acs.c I would still doubt "curses.h will map them" from the man page's wording that curses uses the defaults.

claim: If n is negative, then the entire string will be added
quote: HOWTO:1772-1773: "If n is negative, then the entire string will be added." curs_addstr.3x: "If n is -1, waddnstr writes the entire string."
earlier: The HOWTO sentence alone looked plausible; the man page confirms it for addnstr/waddnstr.

claim: It gives the number of columns and the number of rows in a given window
quote: HOWTO:1745-1746: getmaxyx "gives the number of columns and the number of rows in a given window." curs_getyx.3x: getmaxyx stores the window's maximum valid line and column dimensions in y and x.
earlier: I would have said the same after the HOWTO line; the man page only confirms dimensions rather than corner coordinates.

claim: let's interact with world; message to be appeared on the screen; Try resizing your window(if possible); ch(of type char); the character printed ... until it is turned off
quote: HOWTO:1539 "let's interact with world"; :1721 ": message to be appeared on the screen"; :1729 "Try resizing your window(if possible)"; :1588-1589 "character ch(of type char)"; :1602-1604 "the character printed in the window are associated with the attributes until it is turned off."
earlier: "message to be appeared" alone shows the printed text is wrong; the other fragments are the same class of error.

claim: With _DEBUG defined, print_win_params() prints at row 25, below the bottom of a 24-row screen, so nothing is shown
quote: print_win_params under #ifdef _DEBUG does mvprintw(25, 0, ...). The same HOWTO's key example centers with starty=(24-HEIGHT)/2, i.e. a 24-row screen whose valid rows are 0..23, so row 25 is off-screen.
earlier: Seeing mvprintw(25,0) without the 24-row convention I would have said can't tell; the (24-HEIGHT)/2 usage in the same document settles it.

claim: char str[80]; ... getstr(str);
quote: HOWTO example has "char str[80];" and "getstr(str);". curs_getstr.3x: "int getstr(char * str);" — valid usage.
earlier: The example matched the man prototype on first read; no later source changed that.

claim: Example 4. A Simple scanw example
quote: HOWTO:1908 titles the listing "Example 4. A Simple scanw example" but the body calls getstr(str), not scanw.
earlier: The title alone looked suspicious; reading the listing shows getstr, which contradicts the title.

claim: These pseudo-line-oriented functions turn on echoing while they execute
quote: ncurses-intro.html:778-779: "These pseudo-line-oriented functions turn on echoing while they execute." lib_getstr.c calls noecho() and only waddch-echoes when save_flags._echo was already TRUE; curs_getstr.3x: echoing happens "If the screen's echo option is enabled".
earlier: The intro sentence alone would be matches; lib_getstr.c shows they do not force echo on.

claim: begin read them; must used; one or the other has to changed; The resulting string of characters are pointed to
quote: HOWTO:1826-1828 "begin read them only after..." and "must used so that characters are immediately available"; HOWTO:1895-1897 "The resulting string of characters are pointed to by str"; ncurses-intro.html:770-771 "one or the other has to changed before calling getch()".
earlier: Each fragment is independently ungrammatical; opening the second file only adds more of the same.

claim: Initially RED color is defined with content 1000(r), 0(g), 0(b); init_color(COLOR_RED, 700, 0, 0) is described as lightening red by a minuscule
quote: HOWTO:2690-2695 says use init_color(COLOR_RED, 700, 0, 0) to "lighten the intensity of red color by a minuscule" and :2703-2704 "Initially RED color is defined with content 1000(r), 0(g), 0(b)". lib_color.c sets COLOR_RED to RGB_ON=680; curs_color.3x notes ncurses uses 680 (SVr4 used 1000). 700 from 1000 is darker, not lighter.
earlier: The lighten-vs-700 inconsistency is visible in the HOWTO alone; lib_color.c further contradicts the 1000 initial value for ncurses.

claim: attr_get() is useful in scanning areas of screen when we are not sure what attribute each character is associated with
quote: HOWTO:2107-2112 claims attr_get is useful when "we are not sure what attribute each character is associated with". curs_attr.3x: wattr_get retrieves attributes for the given window (the window's current attribute), not per-cell attributes.
earlier: Before the man page I might have accepted the HOWTO use-case; wattr_get's window-level description contradicts scanning each character.

claim: Other functions wchgat(), mvchgat(), wchgat() behave similarly
quote: HOWTO:2163: "Other functions wchgat(), mvchgat(), wchgat() behave similarly". Man lists chgat, wchgat, mvchgat, mvwchgat — the HOWTO repeats wchgat and omits mvwchgat.
earlier: The duplicated wchgat in the HOWTO sentence is already enough; the man page shows the missing mvwchgat name.

claim: /* pager functionality by Joseph Spainhour" <spainhou@bellsouth.net> */
quote: HOWTO:1957 comment reads: /* pager functionality by Joseph Spainhour" <spainhou@bellsouth.net> */ with a stray quote after the name.
earlier: That single line is the whole claim; no further source needed.

claim: screeen; are we are at; cut bold on; Forth parameter; Viola !!!; loose track; the the source; Don't worry about all those initialization and other crap
quote: HOWTO contains "screeen" (:1979), "are we are at" (:1984), "cut bold on" (:1994), "Don't worry about all those initialization and other crap" (:2013), "loose track" (:2091), "Forth parameter" (:2192), "Viola !!!" (:2631), "the the source" (:2660).
earlier: "screeen" alone establishes defective printing; the rest of the list matches further hits.

claim: mvprintw(24, 0, "Character pressed is ..."); mvprintw(23, 0, "You chose choice ...")
quote: Example uses starty=(24-HEIGHT)/2 then mvprintw(24, 0, "Character pressed is = ...") and mvprintw(23, 0, "You chose choice ..."). On a 24-row screen valid rows are 0..23, so row 24 is off-screen.
earlier: mvprintw(24,...) with an explicit 24-row layout is already enough; line 23 is at the last on-screen row and can be overwritten by scrolling concerns but row 24 is clearly wrong.

claim: startx = (80 - WIDTH) / 2; starty = (24 - HEIGHT) / 2;
quote: HOWTO hard-codes 80 and 24. LINES/COLS are the library's screen size (lib_setup.c exports LINES); the printed example ignores them.
earlier: Hard-coded 80x24 is already incorrect for a general ncurses program; LINES/COLS documentation only confirms the right alternative.

claim: the Functions keys; See the initialization section; if(ch == KEY_LEFT); User did a choice come out of the infinite loop
quote: HOWTO:2742 "get the Functions keys"; :2743 "See the initialization section for details"; :2768 "if(ch == KEY_LEFT)"; :2874 "User did a choice come out of the infinite loop". KEY_LEFT itself is valid; the surrounding printed English is not.
earlier: The comment at :2874 alone is broken English; the other fragments are consistent with that.

claim: The default is one fifth of a second
quote: HOWTO:3138 "The default is one fifth of a second." curs_mouse.3x: "The mouse interval is set to one sixth of a second". DEFAULT_MAXCLICK is 166 (~1/6 s).
earlier: After only the HOWTO I would have said matches; the man page and DEFAULT_MAXCLICK contradict "one fifth".

claim: if (event.bstate & BUTTON1_PRESSED) with mousemask(ALL_MOUSE_EVENTS, NULL)
quote: Example calls mousemask(ALL_MOUSE_EVENTS, NULL) and tests BUTTON1_PRESSED. ALL_MOUSE_EVENTS is defined as (REPORT_MOUSE_POSITION - 1) and includes press bits; the combination is valid.
earlier: Same conclusion after reading the example; headers only confirm ALL_MOUSE_EVENTS covers BUTTON1_PRESSED.

claim: report_choice(event.x + 1, event.y + 1, ...); j = starty + 3; mouse_x <= i + strlen(...)
quote: report_choice sets j = starty + 3 while print_menu places the first choice at menu-local y=2 (screen row starty+2). It also passes event.x+1, event.y+1 though MEVENT x,y are already screen coordinates. The printed hit-test math does not match the menu layout.
earlier: The +1 on event coordinates alone looked wrong after reading curs_mouse.3x; comparing j=starty+3 to print_menu's y=2 confirms a second layout bug.

claim: startx = (80 - WIDTH) / 2; starty = (24 - HEIGHT) / 2; mvprintw(23, 1, ...); mvprintw(22, 1, ...)
quote: Mouse menu example hard-codes startx=(80-WIDTH)/2 and starty=(24-HEIGHT)/2, then uses mvprintw(23,1,...) and mvprintw(22,1,...). Same fixed 80x24 assumption as the key example; not correct for arbitrary LINES/COLS.
earlier: Hard-coded 80 and 24 already decide it; the mvprintw rows are merely consistent with that assumption.

claim: The event mask table stops at BUTTON4_TRIPLE_CLICKED
quote: HOWTO table's last BUTTON*n* line is BUTTON4_TRIPLE_CLICKED before BUTTON_SHIFT/CTRL/ALT. include/curses.tail and curs_mouse.3x also define BUTTON5_* masks. The printed table is incomplete.
earlier: Noticing the HOWTO ends button numbers at 4 would be can't tell without headers; BUTTON5_* in curses.tail shows the printed table is wrong/incomplete.

claim: lets do the same thing from mouse; any thing; a class of mouse events have been enabled; Do some thing; thousands of a second; convert to mouse co-ordinates to screen relative
quote: HOWTO:2894 "lets do the same thing from mouse"; :2904 "any thing else"; :2954 "Once a class of mouse events have been enabled"; :2966 "Do some thing with the event"; :3131 "convert to mouse co-ordinates to screen relative"; :3135 "thousands of a second".
earlier: Any one garbled phrase suffices; the section is full of them.

claim: getbegyx() and getmaxyx() store the window's beginning and maximum co-ordinates
quote: HOWTO:3178-3179: "store current window's beginning and maximum co-ordinates." curs_getyx.3x: getbegyx stores the origin; getmaxyx stores maximum valid line and column dimensions ("one more than the corresponding maximum positions"), not a maximum coordinate pair in the same sense.
earlier: The HOWTO wording sounds plausible; the man page's dimension-vs-position distinction contradicts calling getmaxyx's results "maximum co-ordinates".
